title_question: Why doesn't AI know about my files?
one_liner: RAG lets an AI look up the right pages from your own documents before answering, so it answers from them instead of guessing.

steps.title: Documents are chopped into chunks
steps.text: Your PDFs and notes are split into short sections (typically a couple of paragraphs each) and converted into numerical meaning fingerprints.

stage_state.description: Large multi-page document divides into organized color-coded text cards.

steps.title: You ask a question
steps.text: When you type a query, the system transforms your question into the same mathematical representation to compare topics.

stage_state.description: User query card aligns with similarity coordinate space.

steps.title: The most relevant chunks are retrieved
steps.text: A search engine pulls the three to five paragraphs whose meaning most closely matches your question, skipping irrelevant chapters.

stage_state.description: Target paragraph cards fly forward with glowing relevance scores.

steps.title: AI answers using those passages with citations
steps.text: The AI receives the retrieved passages alongside your prompt and drafts an answer referencing those exact excerpts.

stage_state.description: Answer appears with clickable citation badges pointing to source page numbers.

analogy.text: Think of it like an open-book exam with a helpful research librarian. Instead of forcing a student to memorize an entire library, the librarian pulls the exact three relevant pages and sets them on the desk before the student writes an answer.
analogy.breaks: The librarian can occasionally select the wrong page, the AI reader can misinterpret dense phrasing, and the resulting response remains only as accurate as the source documents you supplied.

myth.claim: RAG eliminates all false statements and mistakes from an AI response.
myth.reality: RAG significantly grounds responses and reduces imaginative errors, but a model can still misread excerpts or answer poorly if key context is missing.

seen_in: Google NotebookLM answering questions from your uploaded PDFs
Company internal search assistants in Notion, Slack, or Google Drive
Customer support chatbots answering questions using official help center articles

persona_examples.student: Asking for a quiz strictly based on chapter 4 of your biology textbook, citing specific page numbers.
persona_examples.teacher: Drafting parent communication letters based directly on your school district's published handbook rules.
persona_examples.entrepreneur: Answering client product questions directly from your current price sheet and service agreements.
persona_examples.engineer_office: Querying engineering specifications across hundreds of archived internal architecture proposals.

quiz.question: What is the primary role of the retrieval step in a RAG pipeline?
options: To retrain the neural network on the internet
To locate and extract the most relevant passages from your private files before answering
To encrypt the user's hard drive
To format the output as a PDF file
quiz.explanation: Retrieval finds the pertinent paragraphs from your documents and hands them to the language model as context.

quiz.question: If a RAG assistant provides an inaccurate answer, what should you examine first?
options: Check whether the correct document chunk was retrieved and whether your source document contained up-to-date facts
Restart your computer and replace your keyboard
Assume the model has developed consciousness
quiz.explanation: Most RAG failures stem from missing the relevant passage during retrieval or outdated facts in the uploaded files.

quiz.question: Does applying RAG guarantee that a model makes zero factual mistakes?
options: Yes, RAG guarantees 100 percent flawless accuracy in all situations
No, while it grounds answers in real excerpts, models can still misinterpret passages or struggle with confusing phrasing
Yes, because retrieval disables the neural network
No, because RAG only works on fiction novels
quiz.explanation: RAG anchors responses to source text, but careful review is still prudent because models can occasionally misread details.

explain_back.prompt: Complete this sentence to prove you understand:
explain_back.template: RAG works like a research assistant who pulls the right pages first, then the AI writes an answer based on those excerpts with source links.

bullets: Chunking strategies (fixed-size, semantic, or recursive character splitting with overlap) balance granularity against context continuity.
Embedding models encode chunks into vector spaces where cosine similarity measures conceptual proximity.
Hybrid search combines dense vector retrieval with sparse keyword matching (BM25) to capture both semantic intent and exact acronyms.
Rerankers (cross-encoders) rescore top candidates, and assembled prompts include citations with strict grounding instructions.

code_panel.title: Minimal RAG Query Pipeline
code_panel.code:
# 15-line production RAG query flow (pseudocode)
def answer_with_rag(query: str, vector_store, llm):
    # 1. Embed query and retrieve top passages
    query_vec = embed_model.get_vector(query)
    candidate_chunks = vector_store.similarity_search(query_vec, top_k=5)
    
    # 2. Re-rank passages for maximum precision
    reranked = reranker.rank(query=query, passages=candidate_chunks)[:3]
    
    # 3. Assemble prompt with grounded context
    context_block = "\n\n".join([f"[Source {c.doc_id}]: {c.text}" for c in reranked])
    prompt = f"Context:\n{context_block}\n\nQuestion: {query}\nAnswer based only on context:"
    
    # 4. Generate grounded completion
    return llm.generate(prompt)
